about: Clay's head as fitted architectural pieces (see head_sheets.md): an orange face mass, a dark roof shell fitted over it whose back corners continue as the horns, a nose crest on the front of the roof, a hinged jaw, eyes with lids hinged on the canthal axis, and ear frills tucked under the horns. Model units: z = (700 - px) / 343, y = (830 - py) / 343, from the 1400 px side reference; x = Clay's left.

upper_head.note: The orange face mass under the roof. Top line is the measured side silhouette less the roof thickness; lower edge is the upper lip in front and, behind the mouth corner, the cheek's lower edge, which curves in (concave) and then up to end under the ear opening.

lower_jaw.note: Set back under the overhanging upper lip (strong overbite); chin juts forward and down. Its top edge follows the mouth line: low and nearly level to the mouth corner under the eye, then an inward (concave) curve back and up to end under the ear opening.

dark_plate_edge.note: Eave line of the roof: the height (y) its lower edge reaches. At the front the roof covers the muzzle down to the lip; its edge rises steeply in front of the eye, steps up over the eye (the eye sits tucked under the eave), and runs back level to the horns.

eye.note: Round, wide-open eye tucked under the eave. The canthal axis (tear duct at the front-lower corner to the back corner where the creases meet) rises about 26 degrees toward the back in the side view; the lids are shells hinged on that axis, so a blink sweeps the upper lid forward-down across the eye.

horn.note: Not a cone planted on the skull: the horn is the back corner of the roof drawn out. It starts embedded in the roof's top shoulder above the eye, runs back along the roof (its top line continues the roof's top line in the side view), leaves the skull behind the brow, sweeps back nearly level and curves gently up at the tip.

ear_frill.note: Sits at the back of the cheek under the horn; its top (front) edge rolls over and curves back to meet the underside of the horn.

roof.note: A shell fitted over the face mass, standing proud of it so its eave overhangs the orange. Overlapping transverse bands, each thickest at its back edge, like armadillo plates. Its back corners continue as the horns.

nose_crest.note: Its own feature on the front of the roof, above the upper lip: a raised pad with a centre ridge. Each side flares out over a nostril and flattens onto the muzzle plane at the nostril's outer corner. It joins the muzzle at the front between the nostrils and fades into the roof behind.

anatomy.note: Sculpt from the inside out: bone landmarks first, muscle masses over them, then skin creases where muscles meet or skin folds over something that moves. Every entry says what it is and what it does to the surface. Positions are side-view (z, y); offsets act on the side of the face.

bone.name: cheekbone and zygomatic arch
bone.why: The jugal bone runs from below the front of the eye back to the jaw joint under the ear. Its crisp top edge is the floor of the eye socket: the eye and its lower lid pad rest on it. Below, it slopes off gently into the masseter.

bone.name: postorbital bar
bone.why: Closes the back of the socket, rising from the cheekbone to the brow (the roof's eave). It is the firm wall the upper crease runs along.

bone.name: eye socket
bone.why: The bony orbit between brow, cheekbone and postorbital bar; the eyeball sits in it.

muscle.name: orbicularis (lid ring)
muscle.why: The ring muscle round the eye that closes it. It makes a soft raised pad around the lids, longer toward the back corner along the canthal axis; its lower edge is the zig-zag crease and it sits on the cheekbone shelf.

muscle.name: masseter
muscle.why: The jaw-closing muscle from the zygomatic arch down to the jaw: the full rounded cheek above the cream jowl, behind the mouth corner.

muscle.name: lip and snout muscle (levator)
muscle.why: Lifts the upper lip; a gentle fullness on the side of the muzzle in front of the eye, below the roof's eave.

muscle.name: temporalis
muscle.why: Fills the skull behind the eye up to the roof; it is why the cranium under the roof is wide behind the brow. Shaped by the face stations, not a brush.

skin.name: lower lid crease (zig-zag)
skin.why: Where the orbicularis pad meets the cheekbone: measured from the side reference, front-lower to the back corner.

skin.name: upper lid crease
skin.why: The fold where the lid ring tucks under the brow, running back from the eye's back corner along the postorbital bar.

skin.name: masseter fold over the jowl
skin.why: The cheek muscle's lower edge folding over the jowl, parallel to and above the rising mouth line.

skin.name: ear opening
skin.why: The ear opening, just above where the mouth line ends.

skin.name: pit at the eave notch in front of the eye
skin.why: A small pit at the eave notch; not the nostril.
